THE MODULE (143 lines, well under the 250 target)
`runEnvironmentEdge(context): DurableDecision`, serving both kinds. THIN: it validates no name, size, scope or key — environment-store.ts owns all four and their fixed order — and it returns the store's refusals UNRESTAMPED via `new DomainRefusal(refusal.code, refusal.layer, refusal.detail)`, so code AND layer are the store's own. `ENVIRONMENT_EDGE_RESULT_CODES` maps set/unset to ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SET / ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_UNSET.
DISJOINT FROM `requestOf`, and the header says why at the site: `requestOf` encodes the WHOLE envelope including `payload` into the request bytes every bootstrap service persists beside its decision, so taking the shared path would write the operator's secret into durable command bytes on the FIRST dispatch. Same structural reason `preview.decide` and the five graph mutations bypass it.
`EnvironmentEdgeEnvelope` is deliberately NARROWER than RuntimeCommandEnvelope — `{commandId, payload}` only. A correlationId/expectedVersion/principal reaching this module would be one more field a value could be copied into en route to a log line.
WIRE TYPING is the one thing the edge adds: a JSON field typed string can arrive null/number/object. Each refuses at the layer OWNING that field, reusing the CLOSED four-code roster rather than minting a fifth — environment (SCOPE) then name (NAME) then value (VALUE), matching the store's documented choice that a non-string value is ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE.

PLAN ASSUMPTION MEASURED FALSE — "a retried command dedupes in the store instead of double-writing"
It does not replay. First implementation derived `disposition` from `store.getCommandReceipt(commandId)` and the arm RED with the store's own error:
`CommandIdConflictError: COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT: command "cmd-edge-retry" was reused for a different request` at `packages/store/src/event-ledger-transaction.ts:128`.
CAUSE (measured, not guessed): `resolveCommand` compares REQUEST DIGESTS under the command id, and an environment write's digest can never repeat — the set event carries a freshly-nonced seal and both events carry a fresh `randomUUID()` eventId. So a resubmitted commandId CONFLICTS.
RESOLUTION: I did NOT reimplement idempotency at the edge (a receipt-based short-circuit would be an idempotency authority outside the store that owns one, and global rail 1's "assert against the production surface" cuts against it). `disposition` is now always DECIDED, the store's error propagates unwrapped, and the arm asserts the property that actually matters: `expect(conflict).toBeInstanceOf(CommandIdConflictError)`, `.code === "COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT"`, and the aggregate version is UNCHANGED after the retry — i.e. a retried set never double-writes. The arm also asserts the conflict message does not contain the secret (it names the command id only). `refusalFor` (daemon-command-dispatch.ts:171) maps `DurableStoreError` to a 503 refusal carrying `error.message`, so that message being value-free is load-bearing.
